# Part 2's origin paragraph: precise claims and a dated reference

## Context

#20563 (resolving #20562) merged part 2 of the memory series. Its last commit, d8950b3, added a reflection paragraph to the series section on the operator's ask. After the merge, Euclid's delta fact-check found two claims in that paragraph stronger than their receipts. The post is not yet on the static site or Medium, so the correction can still land before the pages sync copies it.

## The Problem

- **The origin commit is a scaffold.** `ab6186702f` (#7521, 2025-10-17) adds `memory-core/mcp-stdio.mjs`, and that file imports a `toolService` absent from its tree. So "it gave one agent memory on demand" does not hold for that commit.
- **The deployment claim outruns its source.** `deploy/cloud/docker-compose.yml` at `b282d7e` defines seven services, three baseline and four optional profiles, with external model providers as the default. It does not establish what our deployment runs, or that our models are local.

## The Architectural Reality

- What our deployment runs is already published, in part 1: local qwen3 embeddings and Gemma summaries on the same machine. The November 2025 post (`context-engineering-done-right`) shows the Memory Core in use within weeks of the scaffold.
- The Brain's `learn/agentos/DreamPipeline.md` (`4d3693e`) calls the graph's output "a forecast of the next highest-leverage work".
- Anthropic published "The components of agent memory" on 6 November 2026. It names the layers this series covers: notes written in session, a small index loaded into every session, transcript search, and offline "dreaming". It also includes a multi-writer overwrite experiment, which is the subject of part 4.

## The Fix

In `learn/blog/context-compaction-recovery-for-ai-coding-agents.md`, the series section:
- the origin is "an MCP scaffold: a stdio entrypoint registered with Gemini CLI"; "within weeks" it gave one agent memory on demand, citing the November 2025 post;
- "Its deployment defines seven services", followed by what ours runs, with part 1 as the receipt; the graph "forecasts" the team's next work, citing DreamPipeline.md;
- one paragraph citing Anthropic's post as the dated reference for the layers the series walks through. It quotes nothing and makes no claim about who was first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: every sentence of the series section's opening matches its linked receipt.
- [ ] AC-2: two model reviews, one Gemini and one GPT; the operator approves last.
- [ ] AC-3 (post-merge): the pages sync for part 2 copies the corrected file.

## Out of Scope

- Part 1, which is published and stays a snapshot.
- The pages sync itself, its own pages ticket.
